context: Sunburst-to-icicle morphing chart of a 3-level org hierarchy (~150 employees across 6 departments), toggling between radial arc and rectangular partition layouts via animated point-resampling interpolation.
first_impression: Structurally honest partition layout with correct proportional encoding, but synthetic random data and no key function in the data join limit rigor.
what_works: d3.partition() correctly encodes values as angular span (proportional at each depth level), so area encoding is mathematically honest; domain is fully data-driven via hierarchy.sum() with no hardcoded maxes.
what_doesnt: No key function in .data(layoutData).join('path') breaks object constancy if data were re-joined; random synthetic values (randInt seeded LCG) mean correctness of relative magnitudes cannot be validated against real data.
